rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a compositional change (reducing Mo by substitution), whereas the hidden target uses thermomechanical processing (cold rolling and annealing) of a fixed composition. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies arc-melting, homogenization annealing, and room-temperature compression testing, while the target uses vacuum levitation melting, cold rolling, and room-temperature tensile testing. The testing mode (compression vs. tension) and processing route differ, placing them in different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced electronegativity difference to ease dislocation motion and enhance plasticity, while the target relies on work hardening, dislocation accumulation, texture, and subsequent recovery/recrystallization. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased plasticity with strength near ~1600 MPa in compression, whereas the target reports tensile strength up to 1408 MPa with reduced elongation after rolling, and strength decrease with elongation increase after annealing. The property direction and testing mode differ.
